items.title: COR-TRY-23-028, Moody's Credit Rating Update
notes:
During the Committee's discussion, Craig Dyer, Commissioner of Corporate Services and Chief Financial Officer, addressed queries regarding the Region's credit rating. He clarified that exceeding the AAA-rated Canadian municipal median in terms of debt burden alone may not jeopardize the AAA rating. Rather, the rating depends on a combination of factors. 

Moreover, he highlighted that Moody's mention of the two-tier regional government review within the province stems from their concern over uncertainties and additional risk associated with overall debt levels and future debt servicing costs, especially in relation to meeting housing targets. 

C. Dyer also explained the contrast between a Double-A and a Triple-A rating, emphasizing the notable difference in interest rates between the two. 

Regarding increasing reserve balances, he explained that the process involves increasing contributions to these reserves and reserve funds as part of the annual budget process.

items.title: COR-TRY-23-030, Five Year Continuity – Tax Stabilization Reserve and Working Funds Reserve
notes:
C. Dyer spoke to the report accompanied by a presentation. The presentation outlined the fall 2023 Debenture Issuance Preview, Moody's Credit Rating Update, and the Five Year Continuity - Tax Stabilization and Working Funds Reserves.

In response to questions from the Committee, C. Dyer addressed inquiries regarding our financial reserves. He noted that in recent years, the Region has tapped into the Working Funds Reserve only once, resulting in the current balance of $10 million. Furthermore, he elaborated on the Tax Stabilization Reserve fund, indicating that its balance was raised from $10 million to $15 million based on the Administration and Finance Committee's assessment of what would be a more suitable balance given the overall levy of the Region.

items.title: Strategic Focus – Responsive and Engaging Public Service
PDL-CAS-12-012, Processing Centre for Automated Speed Enforcement
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner of Transportation Services, and Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, spoke to the report. Their primary emphasis was on the establishment of a processing center for Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) infractions and the proposed expansion of the ASE Program to encompass all school zones within the Region.

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. Goetzke explained that the density of the speed camera network is a critical factor in altering driver behaviour. Theresa Mendler, Manager of Strategic Community Planning Initiatives, responded to inquiries concerning personnel turnover and staffing implications, noting ongoing collaboration with the City of Toronto to further investigate these aspects. She further provided clarification regarding the allocation of net revenue generated by the program.

Mr. Goetzke emphasized the importance of maintaining program consistency and credibility and detailed the measures in place to ensure the continued maintenance of these crucial attributes.

PDL-CAS-12-012, Processing Centre for Automated Speed Enforcement
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the following to support the Council- approved expansion of the Automated Speed Enforcement Program to all school zones within the Region, subject to 2024 budget approval as outlined in report PDL-CAS-012, dated September 12, 2023: Approve the establishment of a Region of Waterloo processing centre for automated speed enforcement infractions; Direct staff to submit the proposed staffing and budget requirements as part of the 2024 Plan and Budget for the associated start-up costs, and the permanent full-time positions necessary for operating the automated speed enforcement processing centre as outlined in the report; and That the Commissioner of Transportation Services, on behalf of the Region, enter into an Amending Agreement amending the current Agreement between Redflex Traffic Systems (Canada) Limited and the Region dated July 16, 2019, to allow for the supply of necessary equipment for the Region to establish the Region of Waterloo Processing Centre, to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the following to support the Council- approved expansion of the Automated Speed Enforcement Program to all school zones within the Region, subject to 2024 budget approval as outlined in report PDL-CAS-012, dated September 12, 2023:

  1. Approve the establishment of a Region of Waterloo processing centre for automated speed enforcement infractions;
  2. Direct staff to submit the proposed staffing and budget requirements as part of the 2024 Plan and Budget for the associated start-up costs, and the permanent full-time positions necessary for operating the automated speed enforcement processing centre as outlined in the report; and
  3. That the Commissioner of Transportation Services, on behalf of the Region, enter into an Amending Agreement amending the current Agreement between Redflex Traffic Systems (Canada) Limited and the Region dated July 16, 2019, to allow for the supply of necessary equipment for the Region to establish the Region of Waterloo Processing Centre, to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor.
